improvements: After an attack newly confirms a DM-100's defeat, the bot stops treating its old position as a lightning threat and drops its related attack plan. Losing sight of the machine alone does not count as defeating it.
incoming_learnings: Retire a matching remembered caster when an accepted attack newly confirms its defeat; disappearance alone is insufficient. A later observed DM-100 remains a separate live threat. Correcting stale threat bookkeeping does not certify safe guard-pull re-entry or sustained mixed-enemy retreat.

review.review: The hero remained alive at full health when the planner exhausted its options. Decision 1095 (log line 3171) observed piranhas and chest 1696 while hungry, carrying food and an unidentified indigo potion but no known invisibility or identification consumable. The persistent chest obligation subsequently prevented descent at decision 1188 (line 3433). The final accepted move advanced the game clock normally (line 3431); this was not a death or frozen execution. The selecting chain reaches pool supplies before ordinary exploration, but unknown-supply preparation rejects hunger, and the existing puzzle-meal exception excludes pools. This is not sufficient evidence for a meal-only repair: an isolated public-state probe still found no qualifying safe unknown-potion test bank with a protected chest round trip after removing hunger. The observed approach includes water and a doorway, which cannot simply be certified as safe experimental drinking ground. Offline reconstruction matched every earlier selected action and reason through decision 1187 and reproduced the terminal blocker; this is reconstructed bookkeeping, not recorded runtime memory. No patch is proposed because neither safe identification nor an admissible replacement test-and-retrieval route has been established. The unfinished chest, hazard checks, and terminal failure label remain intact.
review.learnings: Mandatory pool retrieval needs an executable supply-preparation route, not merely a descent veto. Hunger admission and safe test-bank geometry must be considered together. Do not infer invisibility from potion color or treat a hypothetical protected route as an observed buff.

recommendations.summary: Resolve the pool's unknown-supply preparation gap before mandatory retrieval blocks descent.
evidence: Decision 1095, log line 3171: hungry, full-health hero observes the pool chest while carrying an unidentified potion and food.
Decision 1187, log line 3431: accepted movement advances the clock with the hero still at full health.
Decision 1188, log line 3433: unfinished piranha chest causes planner exhaustion.
recommendations.reason: Source browsing and selection reconstruction resolved the missing controller chain, but no safe replacement action was established. Validated-state probes at decisions 1095 and 1188 found only two budgeted trip origins: approach water and the entrance doorway. Both failed unknown-test and stash admission; removing hunger or requesting the existing revisit produced no preparation action. No identification resource was observed. Next, build a reduced fixture of this exact approach and establish either an observation-backed identification method or a safe remote test/stash route with a verified protection budget. Relaxing water-bank checks, guessing the potion, or releasing the chest obligation would not be a safe focused repair.
